item.text:
**1B.3 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: I found **one weakly positive, non-nuclear-specific procedural safeguard** and **more substantial evidence of readiness signaling and escalation**, but I did **not** find clear 2024 evidence that Putin materially strengthened nuclear command-and-control safety, custody, or accident-prevention safeguards.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 1B.3 | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, respond to alarm activations in weapons-storage areas, and specify actions for nuclear, chemical, and biological attack scenarios. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of tighter discipline and custody procedures, but it is broad military regulation rather than a nuclear-force-specific safeguard. | 1B.3 |
| Against 1B.3 | `Putin orders tactical nuclear weapon drills to deter the West` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-05-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-to-practice-tactical-nuclear-weapon-scenario-to-deter-west--defence-ministry-3419973 | Russia announced tactical nuclear deployment drills after claiming Western threats. The emphasis is on deterrent posture and operational practice, not on reducing accident risk or tightening custody safeguards. | 1B.3, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Against 1B.3 | `Russia begins second stage of tactical nuclear weapon drills with Belarus` | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-begins-second-stage-of-tactical-nuclear-weapon-drills-with-belarus-3478894 | Reuters reported a second drill phase with Belarus to practice tactical nuclear deployment. The report shows expanded readiness training and cross-border operationalization, but not a new safety or command-discipline safeguard. | 1B.3, 1B.1, 1B.2 |
| Weakly for 1B.3 | `Rússia faz exercícios militares para testar uso de armas nucleares` | Reuters / UOL | 2024-06-13 | https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/06/13/russia-faz-exercicios-militares-para-testar-uso-de-armas-nucleares.htm | Reuters reported that Russia’s elite nuclear unit said the drills would be analyzed so improvements could be made, and that fake warheads were delivered to forward storage points. This is the best evidence I found for procedural learning and custody handling, but it is still exercise-driven readiness rather than a clear safety reform. | 1B.3, 1B.1 |

**Synthesis**

- The **strongest affirmative evidence** is the March 1 military-statute amendment, because it explicitly covers incident prevention, weapon control, and alarm-response procedures.
- The **broader 2024 pattern** is still one of nuclear readiness drills, deployment practice, and deterrence messaging.
- I did **not** find a clear 2024 Putin action that specifically tightened nuclear command-and-control safeguards in the narrow sense of de-alerting, custody hardening, safety redesign, or accident-prevention reform.
- **Search gap:** public 2024 material appears to be thin on internal nuclear safety/custody procedures; what is visible is mostly doctrine, drills, and deterrence signaling rather than concrete safeguard upgrades.
